Erik Ninn-Hansen (17 May 1922 – 20 September 2014) was a prominent Danish politician known for his role in the Conservative People's Party. His political career spanned across several decades during which he held various key governmental positions in Denmark. Notably, he served as the Minister of Justice from 1968 to 1971 under Prime Minister Hilmar Baunsgaard and again from 1982 to 1989 under Prime Minister Poul Schlüter.

Born in Frederiksberg, Denmark, Ninn-Hansen graduated from the University of Copenhagen with a degree in law in 1948. Before engaging deeply in politics, he worked in the legal profession. His political journey saw him elected to the Danish Parliament (Folketinget) as a representative of the Conservative People's Party. Within the party, he was seen as a traditional conservative and held significant influence.

His career, however, was severely marred by his involvement in the Tamil Case (Tamilsagen), a major political scandal in Denmark during the late 1980s. Under his tenure as Minister of Justice, it came to light that Ninn-Hansen had prevented the family reunification of Tamil refugees contrary to the recommendations of the Immigration Service and the Refugee Board. This led to accusations of him misusing power for political or ideological purposes.

The scandal emerged publicly in 1987 and led to a significant political crisis known as the Tamilgate. It resulted in the establishment of the Tamil Commission in 1988 to investigate the matter. The findings of the commission led to immense pressure, and Ninn-Hansen resigned from his position as the Justice Minister in 1989. The following year, the case also contributed significantly to the resignation of Prime Minister Poul Schlüter.

Further judicial proceedings were held, and Erik Ninn-Hansen was found guilty of misconduct and received a suspended sentence. The scandal and the ensuing legal battles overshadowed his prior contributions to Danish politics, and he remained a somewhat controversial figure until his death in 2014.

Erik Ninn-Hansen's career serves as a potent reminder of the complexities and challenges of political life, where achievements can sometimes be overshadowed by political controversies and ethical judgments.
